D007-D015_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling “off” for about seven months now. At first it was mostly this heavy dullness, like someone turned the volume down on all my feelings. Things that used to matter—finishing a tough shift, getting praise from my charge nurse—barely register. I’m still going to work, but I move so slowly my coworkers comment on it, like I’m wading through water just to get from one patient room to the next. I wake up at 3 or 4 a.m. most days and just stare at the ceiling; I can’t fall back asleep and I don’t even care enough to try relaxation tricks anymore.

For the last six months I’ve also been convinced that small things are secretly about me—like when two nurses are talking quietly, I “know” they’re discussing how dangerous I am, or a random song playing in the hallway feels like it’s sending me a message. I sometimes see a man in dark scrubs standing at the end of the corridor or in my apartment, but when I look properly, he’s not there.

There was a stretch about a month ago, maybe two or three weeks, when that numb, slowed-down feeling actually lifted a bit—I could laugh with a coworker—but the sense that people were sending me signals and the shadowy man at the end of the hall were still there, just as strong.
D007-D015_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h002.question:
I’ve been feeling very low for about seven months now. Since my husband died, it’s like the light went out. I used to enjoy my garden club and church choir, but I’ve stopped going. I mostly sit in my chair and stare at the TV without really watching. Everything feels heavy, even talking; sometimes it takes me a long time to answer when my daughter asks a simple question at dinner. Nights are the worst — I lie awake for hours, my mind going in circles, unable to fall asleep.

For the past six months, I’ve also been convinced my husband was seeing another woman before he died. I know it sounds odd, especially since he’s gone, but I feel sure he was sneaking around, even though I can’t point to any proof. I sometimes see a woman in the hallway or sitting on the edge of my bed, or figures standing in the garden, but when I focus, they vanish.

There was a stretch, maybe three weeks, when my mood wasn’t so low — I didn’t feel quite as sad — but those visions and the certainty about his cheating kept going, just as strong, even then.
D007-D015_h002.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h003.question:
I’m a wedding planner, so usually my life is all about joy and details, but for about seven months now I’ve just felt…flat and heavy. I wake up around 3 or 4 a.m. almost every day and just lie there, staring at the ceiling, feeling this constant sadness. Things that used to light me up—tastings, venue walk-throughs, seeing the bride in her dress—don’t do anything for me anymore. My body feels slowed down, like I’m moving through syrup; even walking from the car to a venue feels like a chore. It’s gotten bad enough that I’ve cut back on taking new clients.

At the same time, for about six months I’ve been convinced I have this special calling, like I’m meant to orchestrate events on some huge, world-changing level, beyond regular weddings—almost like I’m chosen. I also keep smelling smoke or this weird chemical scent when no one else can smell it, even in totally different locations.

There was actually a stretch, maybe three weeks long a couple months ago, where my mood didn’t feel particularly low—I wasn’t happy, but not deeply depressed either—yet I still felt completely certain about this “special mission” and kept smelling that same strange odor.
D007-D015_h003.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h011.question:
It started about seven months ago. At first it was mostly this heavy, gray feeling, like the joy just dropped out of my life. I used to love layovers in new cities, going out with the crew, even just watching the clouds from the jump seat. Now it all feels flat, like I’m just going through motions. I barely see friends anymore; I call in sick a lot because I can’t face passengers.

I’m restless all the time—pacing in my apartment, picking at my arms until they’re raw, unable to just sit on the couch. I feel horribly guilty about everything: if a flight is delayed, I’m convinced it’s my fault; if a passenger looks upset, I obsess that I did something terrible and deserve whatever bad happens next. A couple months ago I collected a bunch of my anxiety meds planning to take them all; I even wrote a note. My roommate walked in before I did it.

Around the same time, strange things started happening. I’ll feel fingers brushing my arm or something crawling on my skin when nothing’s there, even when my mood isn’t that low. I’m sure announcements on the PA or comments from passengers are secretly about me, like they’re sending messages. Sometimes my thoughts go off track when I’m talking—I’ll start answering you and suddenly I’m explaining the airline’s uniform policy or some story from a flight that doesn’t really relate.

There are moments, especially on overnights, when I get oddly goofy—like giggling, making silly faces at myself in the galley mirror, doing little dances—totally out of place for the situation. A few weeks back, my mood actually lifted for a bit, but the feeling of being touched and the sense that people were talking in code about me kept going, even without the sadness. Then the depression came crashing back and it’s been dominating most of this whole stretch.
D007-D015_h011.options:

    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h012.question:

When I’m alone, my face pulls into weird expressions without me meaning to; my kids joke I’m making scary faces for no reason.

Most days I can’t enjoy anything anymore — not football, not driving, not seeing my kids. I move slow, like I’m underwater, taking ages to get out of the car or count change. D007-D015_h013.question:

D007-D015_h014.question:

A couple of times he found me in a rigid, odd position on the couch, arm half raised, and I just stayed like that until he moved me; I felt stuck but didn’t fight it.

These “being watched” feelings and the skin crawling have also happened during a two‑ or three‑week stretch when my mood wasn’t especially low—I could function a bit better then—but the sense of being monitored and those weird body sensations never really went away. D007-D015_h014.options:
